ai.title: agent-validation rejects empty schema objects
ai.summary: convertInputSchema now throws on empty or non-object inputPromptSchema and paramsSchema instead of silently skipping. Validation checks typeof and Object.keys length before Zod conversion. Error messages updated to require non-empty JSON schema objects. Affects common/src/templates/agent-validation.ts.

eli5.text: Starting today, if you write a configuration for the assistant that includes an input schema (the rules describing what information the assistant should expect), the system will now stop you right away with a clear error message if that schema is missing, empty, or not written as a proper set of rules. Previously, the system would quietly ignore an empty or invalid schema, which could lead to confusing behavior later on. This affects anyone defining custom assistants or configurations that rely on input schemas, ensuring they provide valid, non-empty rule sets upfront instead of discovering problems downstream.

ai.title: pluralize() f/fe rule reorder + credit/user noun casing
ai.summary: common/src/util/string.ts pluralize() now checks f/fe endings before y and sibilant rules. Prevents words like 'roof' or 'chief' from matching the 'ies' or 'es' branches first. Call sites in web/src/app/orgs/[slug]/analytics/page.tsx, usage/page.tsx, and auto-topup/credit-purchase forms switch 'Credit' and 'User' to lowercase 'credit' and 'user'. packages/code-map/src/parse.ts and scripts/calculate-dau.ts, export-user-emails.ts adopt pluralize() for log output.

eli5.text: Words like 'roof,' 'chief,' and 'leaf' now pluralize correctly (e.g., '2 rooves') instead of incorrectly becoming '2 roofs' or misfiring on other rules. On your screen, you’ll see lowercase 'credit' and 'user' instead of capitalized 'Credit' and 'User' in organization analytics, usage, and credit purchase pages. Internal logs now use the same pluralization logic (e.g., '1 file' vs '5 files') instead of hardcoded 'file(s)' or 'user(s)' patterns.

ai.title: Fix slash command filtering to include commands with empty commandText
ai.summary: Updated `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to include commands with empty `commandText` in slash command filtering and added alias support. Modified `npm-app/src/menu.ts` to define `baseCommand` and `aliases` for commands like `login`, `logout`, `usage`, and `trace` (renamed from `subagent`). Adjusted `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/subagent-list.ts` and `subagent.ts` to reflect the terminology change from 'subagent' to 'trace' in user-facing messages and comments. This ensures commands like `/help` and `/usage` are correctly recognized and autocompleted despite having empty `commandText`.

eli5.text: When you type a slash command like /help or /usage in the app, it now correctly appears in suggestions and autocomplete even if the command has no extra text. The app also recognizes shorter aliases for some commands (like /signin instead of /login). If you use the trace list, youll notice the messages now say trace instead of subagent. The fix makes sure commands with empty text are not filtered out during autocomplete.

ai.title: Add agent registry unit tests
ai.summary: Added comprehensive unit tests for agent registry in backend/src/__tests__/agent-registry.test.ts. Tests cover getAgentTemplate priority order (local over database), database caching behavior, clearDatabaseCache, and assembleLocalAgentTemplates validation. Mocks @codebuff/common/db, drizzle-orm, and agent-validation modules.

eli5.text: The engineering team added a set of automated checks that repeatedly verify the part of the system that decides which assistant template to load and where it comes from, including which one wins when both a local and a database version exist. The new checks also confirm the database cache can be cleared and that locally assembled templates are properly validated before use. This behind-the-scenes work does not change anything you can do today, but it makes the registry more reliable and catches future mistakes before they reach production.

ai.title: agent-registry test type annotation
ai.summary: Added Record<string, AgentTemplate> type annotation to mockStaticTemplates in backend/src/__tests__/agent-registry.test.ts. Removed mockModule('../templates/agent-list') call. Internal test cleanup.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the automated checks that make sure the software keeps working correctly got tidied up. The team removed an unnecessary setup step and added clearer labels to the test data so the checks run more reliably. You wouldn't notice anything different when using the software today. It's housekeeping done to keep the software stable going forward.

ai.title: Added example agents for code review, testing, and docs
ai.summary: Added three new example agent configurations to common/src/util/example-agents/ to demonstrate progressive complexity. Includes Level 1 code reviewer (Haiku), Level 2 test generator (Sonnet), and Level 3 documentation writer (Gemini 2.5 Pro). Each defines specific tool sets, input/output schemas, and system prompts for their respective tasks.

eli5.text: The project added three ready-to-use helper assistants that you can pick from depending on how involved the task is. The simplest one just reviews your code for obvious mistakes, the middle one writes and runs tests for your code, and the most advanced one reads documentation, searches the web, and builds a plan before writing docs or guides. These helpers come pre-configured with specific skills and tools, so people building on top of this project now have starting points instead of writing everything from scratch.

ai.title: Agent-aware-base replaces sonnet4-agent-builder
ai.summary: New `agent_aware_base` template replaces `sonnet4_agent_builder` as primary agent creation handler. Base agent now spawns specialized builders dynamically. Files: `backend/src/templates/agents/agent-aware-base.ts`, `common/src/constants/agents.ts`, `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/agents.ts`. Migration: existing `sonnet4_agent_builder` configs must reference `agent_aware_base` ID.

eli5.text: When you ask the system to create a new custom assistant for a specific job, it now uses a single smarter base assistant that can spawn the right specialist builder on demand, instead of relying on one standalone assistant-builder tool. Existing configurations that previously pointed at the old builder need to be updated to reference this new base assistant, so any saved setup files will stop working until changed. You would notice this the moment you try to create or edit an agent: the process now flows through one central assistant that dynamically picks the best builder for the task.

ai.title: agent-builder template cleanup
ai.summary: Removed `params` object from `inputSchema` in `.agents/sonnet4-agent-builder.ts`, leaving only `prompt` string. Updated system prompt to remove redundant type definition block. Fixed import paths in `backend/src/templates/agents/agent-builder.ts` to point to `common/src/util/types/` instead of `common/src/util/`.

eli5.text: The internal assistant that writes other assistants now only asks you for a short description of what kind of helper you want, instead of also collecting a long list of extra setup details up front. It also found its configuration files in a new location, so its behind-the-scenes setup is tidier and easier to maintain. Nothing changes the moment you interact with it today, but the cleanup makes it simpler to extend later.

ai.title: Genericize agent examples and config types
ai.summary: Renamed example agents to `example-1.ts` through `example-3.ts` and updated backend loader to filter by `example-` prefix. Removed `parentPrompt`, `systemPrompt`, `instructionsPrompt`, and `stepPrompt` from `AgentConfig` interface. Added `sonnet4-agent-builder.ts` with new prompt structure. Scope covers `.agents/`, `backend/`, and `common/`.

eli5.text: Today, the example agents have been made more generic and the configuration system has been simplified. The example agents (formerly named things like level-1-code-reviewer) are now simply called example-1 through example-3, and the system that loads them will only pick up files with this naming convention, making them clear templates rather than specific use cases. The agent configuration options have been streamlined by removing several prompt fields (parentPrompt, systemPrompt, instructionsPrompt, and stepPrompt) and adding a new, more structured agent builder file that provides clearer guidance for creating new agents. If you looked at the system now, you'd see simpler, more generic examples and a cleaner way to start building your own agents, with the new structure available today but

ai.title: Remove CLI edit agent flow, relocate type defs
ai.summary: Removed the 'Edit Agents' menu option and `startAgentEditFlow` handler from `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/agents.ts`. Custom agent creation now uses `startDirectAgentCreation` instead of `startAgentCreationChat`. Relocated `agent-config.d.ts` and `tools.d.ts` from `common/src/util/` to `common/src/util/types/`. Updated `.agents/sonnet4-agent-builder.ts` to read from the new type paths.

eli5.text: If you open the assistant menu, you'll no longer see an option to edit existing custom assistants. Instead, creating a custom assistant now goes through a single, direct setup process rather than a step-by-step chat. Behind the scenes, two reference documents that define how assistants are configured were moved into a shared folder alongside other similar documents. Live today: anyone who previously used the edit-agents menu will not find it, and custom assistant creation has switched to the direct path.

ai.title: Rename agentawarebase to baseagentbuilder
ai.summary: Renamed the internal agent template identifier and file from `agent_aware_base` to `base_agent_builder`. Updated `AgentTemplateTypes`, `AGENT_PERSONAS`, and related imports across backend templates and CLI handlers. This aligns naming conventions with existing builder patterns.

eli5.text: The assistant that helps you create new custom agents was given a new internal name (changing from 'agent-aware-base' to 'base-agent-builder'), which is now live today. If you watched the screen while using it, you wouldn't notice anything different, the agent still helps you build new agents exactly as before, just under the new name. This is behind-the-scenes naming cleanup that makes the code easier for developers to understand, and it only affects the part of the system that handles agent creation.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.450
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.450 in npm-app/release/package.json. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The software's version number was bumped to 1.0.450, and this release bundles several behind-the-scenes improvements to agent handling: agents now load from the database with stricter validation, empty configuration schemas are rejected instead of silently ignored, slash command filtering now includes commands that have no text, and the agent builder has been cleaned up with new example configurations and renamed internal templates. There are also new unit tests covering the agent registry. If you updated to this version today, the most noticeable change is that empty or incomplete agent definitions will now be caught early rather than failing silently, and slash commands with no associated text will now be recognized. These are internal quality-of-life and stability improvements; there is no new user-facing feature, and nothing visible changes in the interface.

ai.title: file-explorer agent id uses AgentTemplateTypes enum
ai.summary: Replaced hardcoded string literal with AgentTemplateTypes.file_explorer enum reference in backend/src/templates/agents/file-explorer.ts. Eliminates drift risk between agent ID definitions and template type constants. Scope limited to backend agent templates.

eli5.text: The system that tracks which kind of helper agent is which now uses the same built-in label everywhere instead of spelling it out by hand in one spot. This affects developers maintaining the agent setup, not anyone using the tool. If you looked at the configuration, you'd see that one helper's ID is now pulled from a shared list of names instead of being typed out on the line, which reduces the chance of mismatched or duplicated names.

ai.title: Add handleSteps to file-explorer, file-picker, researcher agents
ai.summary: handleSteps generator functions added to .agents/file-explorer.ts, .agents/file-picker.ts, and .agents/researcher.ts. file-explorer now orchestrates parallel file_picker spawns via spawn_agents tool. file-picker and researcher define explicit tool call sequences (find_files, web_search) ending in STEP_ALL. Internal agent config refactor.

eli5.text: The assistants that look at code and search the web now have clearer step-by-step playbooks built in, so they follow a set sequence of actions instead of deciding what to do next each time. The file explorer now launches several specialized file-finding agents at once, each focusing on a different part of the codebase, rather than searching piece by piece on its own. If you watched a session now, you'd see it send out multiple parallel searches and then collect their answers, instead of one long back-and-forth. The change affects internal tooling and is live today.
